find: : { kind, mission, missions, lives: forWorld.lives, enemies: countEnemies(forWorld) };
replace: : { kind, mission, missions, lives: 3, enemies: countEnemies(forWorld) };
why: The topbar LIVES readout is the only projection of `world.lives`, and the constant it is replaced with is LIVES itself (balance.json `lives: 3`) -- so this mutation is invisible to any fixture whose board carries full lives. That was EVERY synthetic build until issue #386: `loop.test.ts`'s fake `levels.world` recorded its `lives` argument into `rec.levelBuilds` and then dropped it, spreading `opts.world ?? createArenaWorld(seed)` without stamping it, while the real `createWorldFor` does stamp it. Measured on a88d39e, before the fake was fixed: this exact mutation left 4008 of 4008 tests green across 170 of 170 test files -- the readout was unpinned repository-wide. The fake now applies `lives: lives ?? base.lives`, and THE STATED RESIDUAL test reads the readout across two builds whose arguments differ (a practice board taking arena.ts's own default, then Continue's run board carrying 2), so a constant can no longer satisfy both. Scoped to loop.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only. COUNT RE-MEASURED for issue #428: 1 -> 2, because the start-boundary suite reads the lives a fresh run was given, which is a second path through the same readout. The failing SET was compared, not the number renumbered. RE-ANCHORED for issue #324's step S6: the readout is a field of the one status projection rather than its own `hud.setLives` call, so the mutation now writes the constant into the payload. COUNT RE-MEASURED for step S6 by comparing the FAILING SETS, not by renumbering: 2 -> 3. The two that failed before still fail -- `campaign-continue lands on the run's own level, with its lives` and `THE STATED RESIDUAL: the menu keeps the abandoned world's enemy count until a board is built`. The third is `refreshes the HUD status from the live world as the game runs`, which this same change rewrote: it used to prove the readout was re-sent by counting pushes, which the whole-projection dedup made meaningless, so it now changes the world under a running session and asserts the pushed number followed. That is a case this diff strengthened, and it happens to see this mutation too. COUNT REMEASURED (issue #323): +1, from the chained Launch-to-next-mission scenario added to `loop.test.ts`. That test walks the whole run, so it is caught by anything that breaks a phase transition, a status push or the run's continuity -- which is why it lands in several of these populations at once. The number moved because a test was added to a scoped file, which is the case an exact `expectFailures` exists to force a re-measure for, not a sign the mutation's reach changed.
